results.result: Five preclinical mouse tumor models (EGI-1, KPC, MMTV-PyMT, mPDAC, MET-1) were characterized for tumor stiffness, ECM architecture, and collagen fiber properties. Tumor stiffness correlated positively with tumor volume in most models and with thick, densely packed collagen fibers, while tumors with thin, dispersed fibers showed lower stiffness despite high collagen content. Stiff regions >40 kPa were identified as biomarkers of intratumor heterogeneity and ECM segregation.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C67 provide comprehensive characterization data from SWE measurements, histology, and SHG imaging across multiple tumor models. The correlations between stiffness, tumor volume, and collagen architecture are supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1. The multiscale analysis provides converging evidence for the relationship between mechanical properties and ECM structure.

results.result: BAPN inhibits LOX enzymatic activity, as demonstrated by significantly decreased fluorescence signals of collagen crosslinks (PYD and DPD) in BAPN-treated KPC tumors compared to controls. LOX stabilizes collagen through formation of these trivalent mature crosslinks.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C72 establish the mechanism of BAPN action through direct measurement of collagen crosslinks using two-photon microscopy (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). The significant reduction in PYD/DPD fluorescence provides direct biochemical evidence that BAPN blocks LOX activity. The mechanism is well-established in the literature.

results.result: LOX inhibition with BAPN reduced mean tumor stiffness in all models except MET-1, with the most striking effects in EGI-1 and KPC models, particularly at late tumor stages. BAPN significantly reduced the percentage of stiff regions (>40 kPa) in treated tumors. BAPN treatment did not affect tumor growth in most models except mPDAC.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C84 are supported by extensive SWE measurements across multiple tumor models and timepoints (Figure 2). The differential responses across models are well-documented with statistical analysis. The lack of effect on tumor growth in most models (Figure 2 supplements) is important for interpreting the therapeutic effects observed later.

results.result: LOX inhibition altered collagen fiber architecture by reducing fiber width in EGI-1, KPC, and mPDAC models (but not MMTV-PyMT), disrupting fiber alignment, and increasing fiber curvature (making fibers less linear and wavier) in all models. LOX inhibition also decreased the surface covered by thick, densely packed collagen fibers, correlating with decreased tumor stiffness.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C99 are supported by detailed quantitative analysis of SHG images and Sirius Red staining (Figure 3). Multiple parameters (width, orientation CV, curvature ratio, dense fiber coverage) were measured systematically across models. The correlations between structural changes and stiffness reduction provide mechanistic insight into how LOX inhibition affects tumor mechanics.

results.result: Ex vivo mechanical measurements confirmed that BAPN-treated KPC tumors were softer than controls, with reduced mean stiffness by plate shear rheometry (1.80±0.51 kPa vs 4.15±1.92 kPa) and AFM (0.82±1.58 kPa vs 1.70±1.66 kPa). AFM revealed that LOX inhibition reduced the heterogeneity in local tissue mechanical properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C102 are supported by complementary ex vivo mechanical measurements using two independent techniques (Figure 4). The consistency between bulk rheometry, AFM nanomechanics, and in vivo SWE measurements strengthens confidence in the stiffness reduction. The narrower distribution of Young's modulus in BAPN-treated samples provides additional insight into reduced mechanical heterogeneity.

results.result: LOX inhibition increased T cell migration in all tested tumor models. In control tumors, T cells migrated slowly (2.3-4.1 μm/min) except in mPDAC where they were nearly static (1 μm/min). BAPN treatment increased T cell displacement in all models, with the most dramatic effect (fivefold increase) in mPDAC. BAPN also increased T cell infiltration in KPC tumors (3-4 fold increase in both stroma and tumor islets).
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C117 are supported by dynamic imaging data from tumor slices (Figure 5). Multiple motility parameters (speed, displacement, straightness) were quantified for hundreds of individual T cells. The differential effects across models and T cell types (exogenous vs endogenous) are well-documented. The dramatic rescue of T cell motility in the nearly static mPDAC model is particularly compelling.

results.result: T cell motility was inversely correlated with tumor stiffness across all models. However, the relationship differed between control and BAPN-treated tumors: in BAPN-treated tumors, there was a steep inverse linear correlation, while in stiff control tumors, T cells appeared arrested above a stiffness threshold. T cell motility is highly sensitive to small variations in stiffness in softer tumors.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C123 are supported by individual mouse-level analysis correlating stiffness with T cell motility (Figure 6). The non-linear relationship in control tumors vs linear relationship in BAPN-treated tumors suggests a threshold effect. This analysis provides mechanistic insight into how stiffness physically constrains T cell migration, though the threshold concept is somewhat inferential.

results.result: In the KPC model, PD-1 blockade alone did not affect tumor stiffness or collagen organization. Single-agent treatment with either BAPN or anti-PD-1 showed only non-significant reduction in tumor growth, but the combination of BAPN with anti-PD-1 significantly delayed tumor progression.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C128 are supported by SWE measurements, SHG imaging, and tumor growth curves (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1). The lack of effect of anti-PD-1 on stiffness/ECM is important for establishing that the combination effect is due to complementary mechanisms. Statistical significance is shown for the combination therapy.

results.result: BAPN treatment alone decreased polymorphonuclear neutrophils and increased MHCII+ tumor-associated macrophages. The combination therapy of BAPN with anti-PD-1 expanded GrzmB+ CD8+ T cells, increased the CD8+/Treg ratio, and increased TNFα, RANTES, and GrzmB levels in tumor supernatants.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C134 are supported by flow cytometry and multiplex cytokine analysis (Figure 7B-H). The immune profiling shows that combination therapy shifts the tumor microenvironment toward an antitumor phenotype. The data support the mechanistic rationale for combining ECM normalization with checkpoint blockade.

results.result: Both LOX inhibition and PD-1 blockade alone increased T cell displacement in KPC tumors to similar extents, and the combination therapy showed the same effects as single treatments on T cell motility.
results.evaluation: Claims C135-C137 are supported by dynamic imaging data (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F). The finding that anti-PD-1 increases T cell motility without affecting stiffness suggests chemokine-mediated effects. The lack of additive effect on motility in the combination is notable and suggests that both treatments may reach a ceiling effect for this parameter.

results.result: In vivo stiffness measurements by SWE were strongly correlated with tumor growth and ECM crosslinking, but negatively correlated with T cell migration across the studied tumor models.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C5 summarize key correlations demonstrated throughout the manuscript. C3 is supported by Figure 1A, C4 by collagen crosslink measurements (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and C5 by Figure 6. These correlations integrate multiple experimental approaches and represent central findings of the study.

results.result: Interfering with collagen stabilization through LOX inhibition reduced ECM content and tumor stiffness, leading to improved T cell migration and increased efficacy of anti-PD-1 blockade.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C9 represent the main conclusions of the study, integrating results from Figures 2-7. C6 is supported by Figure 3, C7 by Figure 2, C8 by Figure 5, and C9 by Figure 7A. The causal chain from LOX inhibition to improved immunotherapy is well-supported by the experimental data, though the mechanism linking stiffness reduction to improved anti-PD-1 efficacy involves multiple factors beyond just T cell migration.

results.result: LOX inhibition has differential mechanical effects depending on ECM architecture, with significant improvement in T cell mobility. Despite minor effects on primary tumor growth with single agents, the combination of LOX inhibition and PD-1 blockade increased effector CD8 T cell accumulation and significantly delayed tumor progression in the KPC pancreatic cancer model.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C45 summarize key findings from the abstract. The differential effects across models (C40) are shown in Figures 2-3, improved T cell mobility (C41) in Figure 5, minor growth effects (C42-C43) in Figure 2 supplements and Figure 7A, and combination therapy effects (C44-C45) in Figure 7. These claims accurately represent the main findings of the study.

results.result: The manuscript provides extensive background on checkpoint inhibitor resistance, the role of ECM and fibrosis in immune exclusion, prior work on stromal targeting strategies, and the rationale for targeting LOX. These claims establish the scientific context and prior knowledge supporting the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C39, C64, C103-C104, C138-C155 represent background knowledge and literature citations that establish the rationale for the study. These are appropriately cited and represent accurate summaries of prior work. While not original findings of this study, they are important for contextualizing the results. The citations appear appropriate and the claims are consistent with established knowledge in the field.
